- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Line or code reference: 121
  Problem: The checker resume prompt instructs the session to `call list_sessions (mine: true, limit: 20)` to find an already-created child session and avoid duplication, but only one page of 20 results is requested. If more than 20 sessions were created after the checker's instructions and the already-started child session falls on page 2 or later, the checker will not see it and may start a duplicate stage or fixer.
  Why it fails at runtime: The CLAUDE.md §26 session limit can create many sessions in the interval between the checker's last instructions and the limit stop. The prompt's `limit: 20` could skip the target session if it appears past the first page. However, the target is extremely narrow: a session whose title matches exactly the one the step would create, created after the checker's last instructions message. In practice this is rare because only one stage session of a given title exists at a time.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Line or code reference: 161
  Problem: Pass 1 reviewer qwen/qwen3.7-plus reported that the `[:MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES]` slice is applied to the string `"{["` rather than the list comprehension result. This is incorrect. The expression `char in "{["` is a boolean containment test: `in` with a string on the right tests character membership, so `char in "{["` returns True when `char` is `{` or `[`. The slice `[:MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES]` is correctly applied to the list `[index for index, char in enumerate(text) if char in "{["]`, not to the test string. No code change needed.
  SEVERITY: NONE (false positive — the slice is correctly placed)
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5 (the code is correct; the pass 1 finding is wrong)
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Line or code reference: _decode_json_text, lines 159-162
  Problem: When the harness's `<other-session>` envelope grows past 50 non-JSON characters before the first `{` or `[`, the `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES = 50` position cap will silently exhaust without finding JSON, raising `InputError` and causing the script to exit 2. The pickup then reports `limit_pending=unknown`.
  Why it fails at runtime: The current envelope format uses a short prefix, but a future harness update that adds more wrapper prose before the JSON payload would cause the selector to reject every valid input file, blocking all usage-limit resumes until the script is updated. The `InputError` message does not name the cap value, making the failure harder to diagnose from the pickup's report line alone.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Line or code reference: lines 121-124, CHECKER_PROMPT template string
  Problem: The CHECKER_PROMPT instructs the resumed checker to "call list_sessions (mine: true, limit: 20)" before any step creates a session, to detect a child session that was created before the limit stopped the checker. The hard-coded `limit: 20` only inspects the first page; a busy account can have more than 20 sessions created after the checker's most recent instructions, so the duplicate-stage guard silently fails and the checker may create a second child session, starting a duplicate stage or fixer.
  Why it fails at runtime: When `len(sessions created after the most recent checker-instructions message) > 20`, the resumed checker will not see the already-created child in the listing and will repeat the session-creation step. The result is a duplicate stage or fixer on the same head.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: README.md
  Line or code reference: lines 1262-1285
  Problem: The inserted usage-limit resume block (10 lines) is placed between the existing sentence "a catch-up wake never schedules another (#4990)." and the sentence "An issue therefore waits up to about an hour before its session starts". In the rendered README, the new block ends with `The stale Routine sweep deletes the resume triggers once they have fired.` and is followed on the next line by `An issue therefore waits up to about an hour before its session starts...`. The anaphora "An issue" previously referred unambiguously to the queue items the pickup was draining; the new block discusses sessions being resumed, so a reader has to infer that "An issue" in the following sentence still means a queue item, not a session.
  Why it fails at runtime: Documentation clarity only; no runtime impact. A reader can misread "An issue" as referring to the resumed sessions and conclude that resumed sessions are still subject to the hour-long wait, when the original meaning was queue wait.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  Line or code reference: 121-124, `CHECKER_PROMPT`
  Problem: The duplicate-session guard checks a single `list_sessions` result limited to 20 and matches sessions only by title.
  Why it fails at runtime: If more than 20 newer sessions appear before the checker resumes, the child it already created can be absent from that result, so the checker repeats the session-creation step. Because the listing covers sessions across repositories and the guard does not compare repository identity, a same-title session for a different repository can also be mistaken for that child. Either case can duplicate work or leave the intended task without its session.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
